SEBoK Supply Chain Systems Engineering, Distilled

Fifth-batch SEBoK distillation, batch 4/5. The prompt-named URL Supply_Chain_Systems_Engineering and the alternate Supply_Chain_Engineering both 404; the discipline lives at Supply Chain Integration and Management (SE-115) and Supply Chain Engineering (SE-133), with cross-readings at SE-027 (ESE) and the SoS-engineering pages. Editorial state is Cluster J D8 internal-migration. SE-188 is the batch's three-scale Cluster B stress-test (Doc 604 §XII three-scale sub-form, §VII.7-promoted to formalization-ready at three instances Docs 681/718/723). Supply chain crosses three scales: intra-organization (single-firm internal supply: receiving, manufacturing, shipping), inter-organization-joint (multi-firm contractual supply chains with prime + tiers of suppliers), and federated-SoS (cross-enterprise supply ecosystems with no central authority — global semiconductor or pharmaceutical supply chains as canonical instances). The three-scale sub-form gains a fourth load-bearing instance and elevates from formalization-ready to formalization-canonical. Cluster A universal-sibling at supply-chain-function (sourcing, procurement, logistics, inventory, distribution, returns); Cluster F longitudinal-pulverization at the supply-chain-record rung (each transaction preserved across the supply timeline); Cluster K V3-as-procedure-binding at the supplier-acceptance gate; Cluster E external-carrier at the standards-body ecosystem (APICS, ISO 28000, SCOR).

II. Source Read

The discipline is dispersed. SE-115 (Supply Chain Integration and Management) supplies the integration-and-management rung: prime contractor coordinating tiers of suppliers under contract, with the supply-chain-as-engineered-system stance. SE-133 (Supply Chain Engineering) supplies the engineering-of-the-supply-chain-itself rung: the supply chain as the system being designed, with logistics, inventory, and distribution as engineering sub-disciplines. SE-027 supplies the enterprise-rung composition (supply chain as one ESE concern). Standards ecosystem: APICS (now ASCM) Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) model; ISO 28000 supply-chain-security family; ISO 9001 quality flow-down; MIL-STD-1916 (supplier acceptance). Six standard supply-chain functions: sourcing, procurement, logistics, inventory management, distribution, returns/reverse-logistics.

III. Structural Read

Cluster B three-scale sub-form (Doc 604 §XII, §VII.7-promoted), batch's anchor stress-test, fourth load-bearing instance. Supply chain crosses three scales cleanly: intra-organization (single-firm internal supply, where supplier and customer are within one organizational keeper), inter-organization-joint (multi-firm contractual supply chains, where the prime-keeper coordinates N supplier-keepers under contracts), and federated-SoS (cross-enterprise supply ecosystems with no central authority — global semiconductor, pharmaceutical, or rare-earth supply chains where the federation has emergent behavior beyond any keeper's authority). The three-scale sub-form previously had three load-bearing instances (Docs 681, 718, 723); SE-188 supplies a fourth at the supply-chain rung, where the three scales co-exist within the same discipline as a span rather than as alternative readings. The three-scale sub-form is now formalization-canonical.

Cluster A universal-sibling lattice, supply-chain-function rung, N=6. Sourcing / procurement / logistics / inventory / distribution / returns is a clean N=6 universal-sibling lattice. The N=6 instance is sub-canonical to the §VII.7 N≈10 marker; convergent with SE-184's six-axis requirement-type lattice. SE-188 reads as a sourcing-side complement to SE-184's specification-side lattice.

Cluster F longitudinal-pulverization at supply-chain-record rung. Each transaction (PO, receipt, ship, return) preserves the substrate (the supply-chain state) across the timeline. This is structurally the same form as SE-186's records management at the supply-chain rung, with the IM-anchor (SE-114) again as the underlying substrate-preservation discipline. Refinement D longitudinal-pulverization at fifth confirming sub-rung after CM/TRA/DE/records (SE-186).

Cluster K V3-as-procedure-binding at supplier-acceptance gate. Supplier acceptance (incoming inspection, first-article inspection, source surveillance) is V3-shaped: the procedure exists because supplier-quality cannot rely on contractual virtue alone, particularly across the inter-organization-joint and federated-SoS scales. MIL-STD-1916 codifies the V3 binding for defense-domain. V3 sub-mode candidate: supplier-binding, ninth sub-mode candidate.

Cluster E external-carrier sub-pattern (D8.1). The supply-chain discipline's authoritative carrier is APICS/ASCM (SCOR model), not SEBoK. The external-carrier sub-pattern reaches a fourth load-bearing instance after SE-126 (design-to-cost), SE-139 (Open SE), SE-184 (requirements specification via INCOSE GtWR). D8.1 is now formalization-canonical at four anchored instances.

Cluster H hypostatic-boundary at the supply-chain-as-system rung. The supply chain is treated as the system-of-interest, not as the deeper economic-network reality. SE-133's "supply chain engineering" stance is functional-surface: design the flow, not the underlying market.
